confusable: Polynesian garlands generally (Tahiti, Samoa)
encounter: placed over the head on arrival; graduations; Lei Day (May 1)
era: 1920s-30s (Matson Boat Days; Lei Day 1928)
made_by: Matson and the Hawaii Tourist Bureau for arriving visitors; Don Blanding for Lei Day; the practice itself is Native Hawaiian
story_lead: The garland is ancient; the arrival ritual was a shipping-line invention

confusable: generic tropical-print shirt
encounter: worn by residents on Aloha Friday and by visitors everywhere
era: 1930s (trademarked 1936); Aloha Friday 1960s
made_by: Honolulu tailors and merchants (Ellery Chun and others) for tourists and residents; Hollywood and Aloha Friday later
story_lead: A Japanese kimono fabric, a Chinese-American merchant, and a name that became a category
notes: Origin is arguable: plantation_immigrant (the makers) vs territorial_tourist (the market). Kept as makers.

confusable: tiki bar; Polynesian-pop generally
encounter: ordered at a Waikiki hotel bar, classically the Royal Hawaiian
era: 1953 (Royal Hawaiian / Matson adoption)
made_by: Trader Vic (Victor Bergeron), Oakland 1944, for a California bar; adopted by Hawaii's hotels for tourists
story_lead: The most-ordered Hawaiian drink is a California import Hawaii adopted
notes: Borderline because most of the world resolves it to 'tiki bar' before 'Hawaii'; kept for the origin story.

confusable: tropics generally; hospitality symbol
encounter: Dole Plantation (Wahiawa); Maui Gold; the pineapple on everything else
era: 1920s-30s (Dole canned 'Hawaiian pineapple'; O'Keeffe 1939)
made_by: James Dole and the pineapple industry, for the mainland grocery market
story_lead: The icon outlived the industry: Del Monte left 2008, ML&P stopped 2009, the Dole Plantation remains as a theme park
notes: Borderline: worldwide the pineapple resolves to 'tropics' first. Kept for the industry story.

confusable: pizza with pineapple; nothing resolves to the place but the name
encounter: not encountered in Hawaii as such; a mainland/Canadian menu item
era: 1962 (Chatham, Ontario)
made_by: Sam Panopoulos, for an Ontario restaurant, named after the canned-pineapple brand
story_lead: A Greek-Canadian, a can, and a name: the pizza defines the class of things named for Hawaii and made elsewhere
notes: Recorded as a FAIL on purpose: it defines a boundary class (siblings: Hawaiian Punch, Hawaiian Tropic). Origin 'external' is PROVISIONAL pending Kim's ruling.

confusable: housedress (plain fabric); passes visually only in Hawaiian print
encounter: worn by residents at church and events; Shaheen-era prints in shops
era: 1950s-60s tourism (garment itself 1820s)
made_by: Missionaries for Hawaiian women (holoku undergarment); Alfred Shaheen and 1950s designers for tourists
story_lead: A missionary undergarment that became the tourist dress, and a Hawaiian word the world kept
notes: Channel coded lexical (clean borrowing); visual is borderline. Origin 'missionary_monarchy' is PROVISIONAL pending Kim's ruling; the era will recur (Kamehameha statue, Iolani Palace, the flag).

confusable: California / Australian surf culture; passes only in composition (longboard + Diamond Head, the Duke statue)
encounter: Waikiki beachboys; the Duke Kahanamoku statue; North Shore in winter
era: 1912-1930s (Duke Kahanamoku; Waikiki beachboys); rebranded by California from 1959
made_by: Native Hawaiians (he‘e nalu); Duke Kahanamoku and the beachboys for visitors; California later for the world
story_lead: Hawaii invented it and lost the naming rights
notes: Surfing itself (kinetic) is a separate row later. Borderline only because of the California confusable.

confusable: small guitar; nothing else once heard
encounter: heard everywhere; Kamaka factory (Honolulu, 1916); every hotel lobby
era: 1879 (Ravenscrag); 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition
made_by: Madeiran plantation immigrants; adopted under Kalakaua; sold to the mainland at the 1915 Exposition
story_lead: The most Hawaiian sound in the world is Portuguese
notes: Passes on all three channels (auditory, visual, lexical); coded by the strongest.

confusable: Polynesian pop / tiki bar generally; the word is Maori-Marquesan, not Hawaiian (ki‘i)
encounter: tiki bars and torches in Waikiki; the International Market Place; contrast with the real ki‘i at Pu‘uhonua o Honaunau
era: 1933-34 (Don the Beachcomber, Trader Vic's); Waikiki adoption 1950s-60s
made_by: Hollywood and Oakland restaurateurs for mainland diners; Waikiki hotels sold it back to visitors as Hawaiian
story_lead: A word that is not Hawaiian, an object made in Hollywood, sold in Waikiki as the real thing
notes: The appropriation case. The real ki‘i (Native Hawaiian) get their own row so the two are never conflated. 'external' broadened: made elsewhere AND attributed to Hawaii.

confusable: South Seas / Polynesian generic; residents read it as a costume error (hula wears pa‘u, ti leaf, never grass)
encounter: luau shows and souvenir shops; not in a halau
era: 1890s-1910s (vaudeville hula girl); Hollywood 1930s
made_by: Gilbertese laborers brought the garment (1870s-80s); mainland vaudeville and Hollywood put it on the hula girl for mainland audiences
story_lead: Hula was never danced in grass: the skirt is Gilbertese and the girl is vaudeville
notes: Kept for the appropriation story, like tiki. Pairs with hula (ic011) as the outsider costume vs the real thing.

confusable: Tahitian ‘ote‘a (fast hips, drums); hula is slower and the hands carry meaning
encounter: Merrie Monarch (Hilo, April); Kuhio Beach hula mound; any halau; luau shows for the outsider version
era: banned 1830; revived at Kalakaua's coronation 1883; Merrie Monarch competition 1971
made_by: Native Hawaiians; Kalakaua for the nation; Hollywood for outsiders; Merrie Monarch for residents
story_lead: The one icon where outsiders and residents hold opposite versions of the same thing
notes: Kinetic channel. Outsider set = hula girl; resident set = halau / kumu / Merrie Monarch. First icon where the two sets diverge on the SAME referent.

confusable: none; a generic volcanic headland at most
encounter: the profile from Waikiki beach; the summit trail; every establishing shot
era: 1920s-30s (Matson postcards and posters); television from 1968
made_by: Nature; named by British sailors 1825 (calcite mistaken for diamonds); made an icon by Matson and the tourist bureau
story_lead: The profile with no confusable, named for a mistake: Le‘ahi, the brow of the tuna
notes: The natural-origin anchor. First candidate for the symbol family: the profile is a single line.

confusable: onigiri; the Spam slab settles it
encounter: any 7-Eleven, Zippy's, L&L; Waikiki Spam Jam (April)
era: 1980s (Barbara Funamura, Kauai, usually credited); Spam itself WWII
made_by: Japanese plantation-immigrant form + military filling; assembled for local lunch counters
story_lead: A Japanese form around a military ration: the plantation and the war on one plate
notes: Hybrid origin: plantation_immigrant (form) + military (Spam). Audience tipping toward both. Origin recoded plantation_immigrant -> local 2026-09-13 (provisional).

confusable: the 'poke bowl' (California fast-casual, 2012+) which globally resolves to 'healthy lunch'
encounter: Foodland poke counter; Tamura's; Ono Seafood
era: ancient (‘ahi poke); shoyu-sesame version 1970s; bowl format 2012+
made_by: Native Hawaiians; local Japanese influence 1970s; California rebranded the bowl for the mainland
story_lead: Hawaii owns the word and lost the format
notes: Poke passes; the poke bowl is borderline (the surfboard pattern in food).

confusable: hamburger steak with gravy; resolves to nothing else once seen
encounter: Cafe 100 (Hilo); Rainbow Drive-In; Zippy's
era: 1949 (Lincoln Grill, Hilo)
made_by: Lincoln Grill (Inouye family) for Hilo teenagers
story_lead: Maximally distinctive, barely recognized: the icon the test could not see
notes: Broke the caption test: high distinctness, low outsider recognition. Prompted the split into distinct + recognized. Origin recoded plantation_immigrant -> local 2026-09-13 (provisional).

confusable: global surf 'hang loose'; Brazil's version; here it means thanks / hello / all good, wider than surfing
encounter: every driver who lets you merge; the official state gesture since 2024
era: 1940s (Hamana Kalili, Laie); 1960s (Lippy Espinda TV ads); 1970s (Fasi campaigns); state gesture 2024
made_by: Hamana Kalili's mill injury; a used-car dealer and a mayor for local TV; surfers for the world
story_lead: Three missing fingers, a used-car dealer, and a mayor: how a gesture became a state's signature
notes: Kinetic. Borderline only because surf culture globalized it.

confusable: none; the confusable is the outsider's joke ('wallpaper paste')
encounter: any luau (outsider version); Waiahole Poi Factory, Hanalei (the real thing)
era: ancient; luau-circuit version 1930s onward
made_by: Native Hawaiians (kalo as Haloa); the luau circuit for visitors
story_lead: The outsider's joke is the resident's elder sibling
notes: Sharpest outsider/resident divergence on one referent so far (pairs with hula).

confusable: none; two scoops rice + mac salad resolves to nothing else
encounter: Rainbow Drive-In, Zippy's, any lunch wagon; L&L on the mainland
era: 1880s plantation kaukau tin; lunch wagons 1930s; L&L export 1999
made_by: Plantation workers of every ethnicity sharing one lunch break; drive-ins for residents
story_lead: The islands' social history on one plate: every ethnicity's dish, one lunch break
notes: 'local' origin (provisional). Symbol candidate: the three-compartment plate.

confusable: none; the white span over the hull
encounter: Pearl Harbor National Memorial; the Navy boat from the visitor center
era: 1962 (dedicated); attack 1941
made_by: US Navy and Congress; Alfred Preis (Austrian refugee, interned on Sand Island 1941) designed it; Elvis's 1961 concert helped fund it
story_lead: The man interned as an enemy alien after the attack designed its memorial
notes: First military row. Symbol candidate: the span in profile.

confusable: frangipani across the tropics (Bali, Thailand, India); passes only in composition: the lei, behind the ear
encounter: any lei stand; the scent on a trade wind; behind the ear
era: 1920s-30s lei trade; introduced 1860 (Hillebrand)
made_by: Hillebrand introduced it; cemeteries kept it; lei sellers and the tourist bureau made it the welcome flower
story_lead: The graveyard flower became the welcome flower
notes: Strongest key is the SCENT: channel axis lacks olfactory (added provisional). Coded visual because a symbol can carry that.

confusable: pan-tropical; Malaysia's national flower is the same red hibiscus
encounter: aloha shirts; hedges everywhere; ma‘o hau hele (the real state flower) almost nowhere
era: 1923 territorial flower; Honolulu hybrid craze 1900s-20s; state flower ma‘o hau hele 1988
made_by: The territorial legislature (1923) and the aloha-shirt printers; the plant is H. rosa-sinensis and local hybrids
story_lead: The state flower is yellow and endemic; the icon is red and Chinese
notes: Origin arguable natural (7 endemic Hibiscus) vs territorial_tourist (who made the red one an icon). Coded by icon-maker.

confusable: Nashville pedal steel; country music took the sound
encounter: hotel-lobby trios; Hawaiian-music radio; the Kekuku marker in Laie
era: c.1889 (Joseph Kekuku, Laie); mainland craze 1915-30s; Nashville from the 1940s
made_by: Joseph Kekuku, a Kamehameha Schools boy, for himself; touring Hawaiian bands for the mainland; country music for the world
story_lead: The sound of Nashville came from Laie
notes: Surfboard pattern in sound: invented here, renamed elsewhere.

confusable: none once heard; often mistaken by outsiders for 'just guitar'
encounter: Gabby Pahinui recordings; slack-key festivals; backyard parties
era: 1830s paniolo guitars; family tunings kept secret until Gabby Pahinui's 1946 recordings
made_by: Hawaiian families retuning Mexican vaqueros' guitars, for themselves; Gabby Pahinui and the 1970s renaissance for everyone else
story_lead: A Mexican guitar, Hawaiian tunings kept secret for a century
notes: High distinct, resident recognition: the loco moco of sound.

confusable: none; the melody resolves to Hawaii instantly
encounter: every departure, luau finale, and film farewell since the 1930s
era: 1878 (composed by Lili'uokalani); recast by the 1893 overthrow
made_by: Lili'uokalani, as a love song, for the court; the overthrow and Hollywood made it the farewell of a nation
story_lead: Written as a lover's goodbye fifteen years before the overthrow, then it became the nation's
notes: Auditory icon with a missionary_monarchy origin: the queen as composer.

confusable: none; the most borrowed Hawaiian word
encounter: every greeting, sign, and airport; the Aloha Spirit written into state law (HRS 5-7.5, 1986)
era: ancient; commercial use from the 1900s (Aloha Tower 1926, the shirt 1930s, the airline 1946)
made_by: Native Hawaiians as a concept; the tourist industry as a brand; the legislature as a statute
story_lead: One word for hello, goodbye and love, then a brand, then a law
notes: Anchor of the borrowed-word density metric.

confusable: in English the word now resolves to Wikipedia, not to Hawaii
encounter: the Wiki Wiki Shuttle at Honolulu airport, where Ward Cunningham saw it
era: 1995 (WikiWikiWeb); Wikipedia 2001; the shuttle 1970s-2000s
made_by: Ward Cunningham named his software after the airport shuttle bus, for programmers; Wikipedia for the world
story_lead: The most-used Hawaiian word on earth no longer resolves to Hawaii at all
notes: Recorded as a FAIL on purpose: a borrowed word that lost its origin entirely. Counts for the density metric, not for the icon set.

confusable: none; the only place visitors are routinely invited to watch land being made
encounter: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park; Halema'uma'u at night; the 2018 Leilani eruption in memory
era: Volcano House 1846; national park 1916; the 1983-2018 Pu'u 'O'o eruption made it continuous television
made_by: Pele in tradition; Volcano House and the park for visitors; Mark Twain (1866) for readers
story_lead: The tourist attraction that is also a goddess and also the newest land on earth
notes: Symbol candidate: the fountain / the red line on black.

confusable: rainbows everywhere; passes only because Hawaii adopted it as identity
encounter: the license plate; UH Rainbow Warriors; Manoa on any afternoon
era: license plate 1991; the UH nickname 1923; 'Rainbow State' nickname
made_by: Nature (trade-wind showers over Manoa); the state and the university for residents
story_lead: The place that put a rainbow on its license plate
notes: Borderline on distinct; the ADOPTION is the icon, not the phenomenon.

confusable: none; the outstretched arm and feathered cloak
encounter: Ali'iolani Hale, Honolulu; the original at Kapa'au; Lei Draping on June 11
era: 1883 (unveiled at Kalakaua's coronation); the original lost off the Falklands and recovered, at Kapa'au since 1883
made_by: Kalakaua and the legislature for the nation's centennial of Cook; the Hawaii Five-O credits for the world
story_lead: The first casting sank off the Falklands; the second stands in Honolulu; the salvaged first stands in his birthplace
notes: Symbol candidate: the arm. The most-photographed statue in the state.

confusable: none; the only royal palace on US soil
encounter: downtown Honolulu; the room where the queen was imprisoned in 1895
era: 1882 (completed); electrified 1886, before the White House
made_by: Kalakaua, for the kingdom's standing among nations; the overthrow made it a symbol of what was taken
story_lead: Electric light before the White House, and a queen imprisoned upstairs
notes: Pairs with the flag (ic031) and Aloha 'Oe (ic024) as the monarchy cluster.

confusable: none; the only US state flag carrying the Union Jack
encounter: every public building; flown upside down as a sovereignty statement
era: 1816 (first version, Kamehameha I); 1845 (eight stripes); state flag 1959
made_by: Kamehameha I, to stand between Britain and America; sovereignty movement recast it after 1993
story_lead: A kingdom's flag that became a state's, and is flown upside down by those who want the kingdom back
notes: The one icon whose meaning is actively contested today.

confusable: flip-flops worldwide; Japanese zori; the PILE AT THE DOOR is what resolves to Hawaii
encounter: every doorstep; every school; the pile at a party
era: 1930s-50s (Japanese rubber zori via plantation families; local brand Locals from 1983)
made_by: Japanese plantation families brought the zori; local culture made removing them at the door the rule
story_lead: The icon is not the shoe; it is the pile by the door
notes: Coded local: the practice, not the object, is the icon.

confusable: the snow cone; the difference (fine shave, syrup absorbed) is the whole point
encounter: Matsumoto's (Hale'iwa, 1951); Waiola; Ululani's
era: plantation era (Japanese kakigori); Matsumoto's 1951; national fame via the Obama family 2000s
made_by: Japanese plantation workers for themselves; Hale'iwa surf traffic and a president for everyone else
story_lead: A snow cone is not shave ice, and every resident will tell you why
notes: Symbol candidate: the cone with three colours.

confusable: Polynesia generally (Tahitian va'a); Hawaii's claim is Hokule'a and Waikiki canoe surfing
encounter: Waikiki beachboy canoe rides; the Moloka'i Hoe; Hokule'a at Sand Island
era: ancient; Waikiki canoe surfing 1900s; Hokule'a 1976 made it a renaissance
made_by: Native Hawaiians; the Outrigger Canoe Club (1908) for visitors; the Polynesian Voyaging Society for the renaissance
story_lead: A tourist ride at Waikiki and, in 1976, the vessel that proved the ancestors navigated on purpose
notes: Hokule'a may deserve its own row.
